---
title: "Pre-Build Workflows"
description: "Configure how Revolte reviews, summarizes, and prepares generated changes before they reach human reviewers."
---

Pre-build workflows let Revolte perform automated review passes and summarize generated changes before they reach human reviewers. Use them to keep pull request descriptions consistent and surface obvious issues early.

## Prerequisites

Before configuring pre-build workflows, make sure you have:

- A Revolte workspace with an application connected
- Permission to edit the application's YAML configuration
- Repository access for the application you want Revolte to review
- Agreement on the pull request summary and review style your team wants

## Open YAML Configuration

To configure these workflows, select your project, open the application, and navigate to **YAML Configuration**. Use the **Repo Preference** tab to manage pre-build behavior.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Select the project">
    From the dashboard, go to **Projects** and open the project that contains the application.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open the application">
    Choose the application repository you want Revolte to configure.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open YAML Configuration">
    Select **YAML Configuration**, then use **Repo Preference** to configure repository and pre-build behavior.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Frame caption="Interface for managing automated review, summarization, and repository preferences.">
  <img src="/images/pre-build-workflow.png" alt="Pre-build workflow configuration screen" width="600" />
</Frame>

## Code Review and Summarization

The **Code Review and Summarization** section defines how Revolte should comment on and document generated changes.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Summarize Intent" icon="list">
    Revolte adds a concise summary of the generated change to the pull request description, explaining the *why* and *how* of the implementation.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Suggest Fixes" icon="wrench">
    If Revolte detects a potential issue during its own review pass, it can leave inline fix suggestions directly on the pull request.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Comment Style" icon="message-square">
    Choose between **balanced**, **concise**, or **verbose** review styles depending on the level of detail your team prefers.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Exclude Files" icon="file-x">
    Specify files or extensions (like lockfiles or generated assets) that should be ignored by the automated review pass.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## When to Use

Use pre-build workflows when:

- You want consistent pull request descriptions across the team.
- You have a complex codebase where an initial automated review pass helps catch edge cases.
- You want to reduce the "review fatigue" of human developers by catching simple issues early.

<Note title="Manual Review Still Applies">
  While Revolte performs an automated pass, these workflows are designed to *assist* your team. Human review remains the final authority before merging code into production.
</Note>
<Note title="Configuration Validation">
  If you encounter errors while editing your YAML, see [Handling Configuration Errors](/docs/build/validation-pipeline#handling-configuration-errors) for how to use the built-in error logs.
</Note>
